title: Latency & Throughput Guardian: Safe Orchestration of Batching/Caching Optimizations
creator: Aisha Kim
description: Goal: Build a runtime orchestration layer ("Guardian") that applies batching and prefix/KV cache configuration recommendations safely across traffic with automated limiters, traffic-aware routing, and anomaly-driven rollback. This ticket scopes the orchestration algorithm, limiters, integration points with the console, and rollout/playbook for staged apply and automatic rollback when latency or throughput SLOs degrade beyond tolerances. The Guardian must operate across hosted and Dedicated deployments and support shadow/apply modes, progressive ramping, and multi-dimensional circuit-breakers (latency, tail, throughput, error-rate).
acceptance_criteria: Guardian can accept a candidate config bundle (batch_size, micro_window_ms, cache_ttl_ms, kv_prefetch) and simulate impact using recent traffic profile
Can perform a staged rollout: shadow -> 1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with automated hold/rollback decisions
Automated circuit-breaker triggers when 95p latency increases > 20% OR p99 latency increases > 10% OR throughput drops > 15% for 5m window
System exposes per-config experiment metrics to Console (cost delta, latency delta, token-per-second, error-rate, rollout cohort)
Rollback completes within 30s of trigger and restores pre-change KV-state/eviction behavior for affected pods
End-to-end tests (integration) covering shadow vs apply, slow-path fallback to compatible smaller batch profiles, and anomaly detection are added to CI
Runbook documented with manual override endpoints and safe-apply toggle for Dedicated customers
design_notes: We will treat the Guardian as a controller in the orchestration plane that emits a series of immutable experiments; each experiment is versioned and linked to a model variant and runtime profile.
Traffic cohorts are created via consistent hashing by customer+route to ensure sticky cohorts across nodes during ramp-ups.
Decisions prioritize latency preservation: optimistic cost savings are constrained by a latency budget window and an emergency 'curtain' that drops batch size to baseline for affected cohorts.
Circuit-breakers are layered: immediate local limiter (node-level), cohort-level circuit, and global safety net. Triggers at any layer initiate rollback for the experiment scope.
We'll use a hybrid anomaly detector: short-window statistical thresholds for quick reaction (5m, 30s granularity) and longer-window trend detection (1h) to avoid oscillation.
KV cache changes include a shadow warming stage where probe requests are served from warmed caches but do not update source-of-truth until fully promoted.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement config simulator + shadow-apply scaffolding and evaluate with historical traffic (2w)
Phase 2: implement cohort assignment and staged rollout engine with per-cohort metrics emission (3w)
Phase 3: add multi-layer circuit-breakers, anomaly detector, and automatic rollback (2w)
Phase 4: integrate with Console for experiment visualization, manual pause/resume, and audit logs (1w)
Phase 5: testing, runbook, and Dedicated deployment checklist (1w)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Aggressive batching reduces cost but increases tail latency; to reduce risk we limit initial batch upsizes and require KV warmup before full promotion.
Shadow-apply doubles some load (probe traffic) during evaluation; for high-traffic customers we will sample fewer requests per cohort to limit overhead.
Automated rollback may mask slow degradations if thresholds are too permissive; we mitigate with dual thresholds (fast and sustained) and post-mortem hooks.

State drift between warmed caches and production cache may lead to inconsistent outputs for certain session-scoped workloads; we will opt-out sensitive routes by config and document expected behavior.
metrics_and_alerts: Key metrics per experiment-cohort: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (reqs/sec and tokens/sec), error-rate, CPU/GPU utilization, cost-per-1k-tokens
Alerting rules: cohort_p95 > baseline_p95 * 1.20 for 3 consecutive 30s buckets -> fire 'guardian:cohort-latency-degrade', AUTO-HOLD
Global alert: global_p99 increased > 10% for 5m -> global rollback
Anomaly scoring: compute z-score on p95 over 1h baseline; if z > 3 and sustained for 2 windows, mark for manual review
Dashboard panels: experiment timeline, cohort map, cost delta heatmap, rollback history
testing_plan: Unit tests for rollout state transitions and circuit-breaker logic
Integration test harness replaying recorded traces with parameterized batch/cache configs
Chaos test: force node-level slowdowns and ensure rollback triggers and restores baseline within 30s
Canary in prod: start with internal-only orgs, then opt-in beta customers before wide rollout
Add contract tests in CI to ensure metrics emission tags and experiment IDs are stable across releases
runbook_and_playbook: On 'guardian:cohort-latency-degrade' alert: guardian automatically HOLDs the experiment; pager notifies on-call if HOLD persists > 5m
If automatic rollback triggered: verify rollback succeeded in Console, confirm p95/p99 recovery; if not recovered within 1m, escalate to runtime on-call
Manual rollback endpoint: POST /guardian/v1/experiment/<id>/rollback with auth header; logs recorded to audit stream
Mitigation steps: reduce batch_size to baseline, disable KV prefetch for affected cohort, increase micro_window_ms conservatively
Post-incident: attach experiment id to postmortem and schedule a follow-up to tune thresholds or exclude problematic routes
